Our people are empowered to continuously improve, deliver outstanding customer service and make a meaningful impact every day. About us  
 At Fenergo, we’re not just building software—we’re transforming how the world’s leading financial institutions fight financial crime. Headquartered in Dublin and trusted by over 100 of the world’s top financial institutions, we’re on a mission to change the game.  
 We’re more than a global leader in AI-powered client lifecycle management—we’re reimagining how financial institutions tackle compliance. From Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) to rapidly evolving regulations, we turn complexity into clarity. Our FinCrime Operating System, powered by agentic AI and intelligent automation, helps financial institutions move faster, act smarter, and stay safer across 120+ countries.  
 But we don’t stop there.  
 At Fenergo, we believe in a world where financial institutions aren’t just compliant—they’re confident. Where technology doesn’t just meet regulations—it stays ahead of them. Our mission is to empower financial institutions to stop financial crime and create a safer world.   
 Every product we build, every innovation we deliver, and every partnership we forge is shaped by that belief. We’re tackling some of the toughest challenges in financial technology. From speeding up onboarding to uncovering hidden risks, our work empowers banks to serve their customers with speed, integrity, and peace of mind.  
 Join us, and be part of a team that’s building smart solutions, solving real problems, and shaping the future—together.  
 What this role entails 
 The Client Success Partner (CSP) is one of the most strategically important client-facing roles at Fenergo. The CSP owns the post-sale relationship outright — retention, adoption, value realisation and growth — and is judged on whether clients keep getting measurable ROI long after go-live, not just at it. The CSP gets alongside the client — in the room, on the hardest problems — because that proximity is where the most valuable work and the sharpest IP are made.  
 Operating that close demands real depth: the Fenergo client lifecycle, the regulatory terrain we work in — KYC, AML, CLM, client lifecycle management, financial crime, risk — and how every team in the firm actually works. The CSP is the person a client’s executives call for a straight answer, and the person inside Fenergo who can get any door opened. 
 Because that depth is hard to hire and easy to grow, the CSP role is first and foremost an internal mobility path. We look for it in people who are already client-facing, product-fluent and trusted internally — Product, Advisory, Client Solutions, Delivery — and move them into partnership.  
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Be the Trusted Partner 
 Own the relationship. Own the post-sale success of a portfolio of clients. Each client has a live success plan tied to a named business outcome and ROI — not a status tracker. 
 Translate, don’t relay. Understand each client’s priorities and pressures and turn them into clear actions for both sides. Communicate hard things plainly; challenge constructively; hold confidence when things are difficult. 
 Run the heartbeat. Lead client success governance — the Monthly Client Pulse with executive sponsors, strategic business reviews and product health checks — as decision-making forums, not read-outs.
 2. Drive Adoption and Value 
 Watch the signals. Track client health, sentiment, adoption and success-plan progress. Use data and stakeholder insight to see risk early, while it is still cheap to fix. 
 Own churn risk end-to-end. Spot at-risk clients and stabilise them at pace with the account team. Adoption depth is the retention mechanism — a live-but-unused deployment is still a churn risk. 
 Be a product partner, not a ticket router. Support functional and use-case questions directly where you can; partner with Product and Support on escalations while keeping ownership of the client experience. 
 Arm the renewal. Give Sales the evidence — value delivered, sentiment, adoption, risk — that makes renewal a formality rather than a negotiation. 
 3. Orchestrate Fenergo around the client 
 Pull the firm together. Coordinate Sales, Product, Delivery, Support and Partners into one joined-up plan. The CSP is the single point where the firm becomes coherent to the client. 
 Be the Voice of the Customer. Feed structured insight back in — needs, adoption barriers, product feedback, growth signals — so the firm learns from every account. 
 Find the growth. Surface qualified expansion, then hand off cleanly to Sales with an account strategy. 
 Own the numbers. Accountable for client-health reporting and the metrics behind it — CSAT, NRR, FTTV
 Required experience and capabilities 
 Experience & Capability 
 7+ years of experience in customer success, account management or a related client-facing role.
 Proven experience in the financial services domain experience, especially with client lifecycle management, onboarding, KYC, AML, FinCrime, fraud, identity, compliance or risk.
 Proven experience building trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, developing accounts into tangible growth opportunities 
 Proven experience managing high risk accounts to resolution at pace, working cross-functionally with Product, Support, Professional Services, Delivery or Sales to resolve client issues and improve outcomes
 Strong understanding of SaaS customer success models, including onboarding, adoption, renewals, retention and expansion.
 Experience supporting renewal, retention and account-growth strategies through value evidence, client insight and risk management.
 Product fluency and problem solving (intelligence) 
 Proven ability to learn a SaaS product and support clients with functional, use-case, enablement and adoption-related questions.
 Strong analytical and consultative problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure complex issues and communicate them clearly
 Experience in implementation, professional services, solution consulting or client transformation programmes.
 Core Behavioural Skills 
 Attitude & Can-do: 
 A positive, solution-oriented attitude is non-negotiable. The CSP approaches every client interaction, internal challenge and setback with a constructive mindset, focused on what can be done rather than what cannot. 
 Curiosity & growth mindset: 
 The best CSPs are genuinely curious about their clients' businesses, about the Fenergo platform, and about the problems they are trying to solve. Curiosity drives better discovery, sharper insights and more creative solutions. It means asking the next question when others have stopped, staying up to date on industry trends and regulatory change, and proactively exploring how Fenergo can unlock new value for clients. 
 Emotional Intelligence 
 Client success is a people business. Emotional intelligence (EQ) is the ability to read a room, understand what is not being said, and respond in a way that builds rather than damages trust. The CSP uses EQ to navigate difficult conversations with empathy and composure, to adapt communication style to different stakeholders, and to recognise when a client relationship needs careful handling. 
 Initiative 
 This role requires sustained energy and pace, the drive to manage a large portfolio, pursue client outcomes relentlessly, and keep momentum across multiple workstreams. Energy is not just about pace; it is about enthusiasm, engagement and the commitment to bring your best to every client interaction and internal collaboration.
 Our promise to you   
 We are striving to become global leaders across all of the categories we operate in and as part of that we are a high-performing highly collaborative team that works cross functionally to accommodate our client’s needs.   
 Collaboration: Working together to achieve our best 
 Outcomes: Drive Success in every engagement  
 Respect: A collective feeling of inclusion and belonging 
 Excellence: Continuously raising the bar 
 What’s in it for you?   
 Healthcare cover with Canada Life  
 Retirement savings plan 
 Employee Assistance Programme  
 Opportunity to earn an annual company bonus  
 20 days PTO  
 3 company closure days 
 Extensive training programs, classroom and online, through ‘Fenergo University’ 
 Other competitive company benefits, such as flexible working hours, work from home policy, sports and social committee and much more 
 Buddy system for all new starters 
 Opportunity to work on a cutting-edge Fintech Product, using the latest of tools and technologies. 
 Defined training and role tracking to allow you see and assess your own career development and progress.  
 Work From Home set-up allowance  
 Diversity, Equality, and Inclusivity  
 Fenergo is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, where all employees are valued, respected, and can reach their full potential. We do not discriminate based on race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Our hiring decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We believe that a diverse workforce enriches our company culture, fosters innovation, and contributes to our overall success. We strive to provide a fair and supportive environment for all employees, promoting equal opportunities for career development and advancement. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply for employment opportunities and join our team in contributing to a collaborative and inclusive work environment. 
 Recruitment Safety

 Employment Type: Full-Time, Independent Contractor

 About the Company 
 Our client is a done-for-you Meta advertising and appointment-setting agency. It supports medspas and aesthetic wellness businesses across the United States. As its client portfolio grows, the agency is hiring a dedicated Client Success Manager to build a consistent, proactive experience for clients after the sale.
 The Opportunity 
 You’ll own the experience of about 40 agency clients. That covers onboarding, campaign launch, ongoing service, retention, and renewal support. You’ll be clients’ main point of contact and the bridge between them and the creative, media buying, appointment-setting, sales, and operations teams.
 This is a client relationship and coordination role. It is not a hands-on media buying position. You’ll also help shape the agency’s first dedicated Client Success function, including the processes and playbook the team will rely on as it scales.
 What You’ll Do 
 Lead structured client onboarding, coordinate handoffs from sales to delivery, set expectations, and document client goals and success metrics.
 Manage a portfolio of about 40 client relationships through scheduled check-ins.
 Respond to client Slack messages within 24 hours on business days.
 Keep CRM records accurate and up to date.
 Spot dissatisfaction and at-risk accounts early, coordinate recovery plans, and support renewals and retention.
 Turn client concerns into clear actions for the creative, media buying, appointment-setting, and operations teams, and follow through until they’re resolved.
 Prepare client-facing performance updates and maintain a portfolio health dashboard that leadership can see.
 Improve onboarding checklists and SOPs, and build a repeatable Client Success playbook.
 Track retention, NPS trends, response times, and onboarding SLAs.
 What Success Looks Like 
 Annual client retention of 93% or higher.
 Every new-client onboarding completed within agreed SLAs.
 Every client contacted according to the established check-in schedule.
 Client interactions logged in the CRM within 24 hours, and churn risks identified before they escalate.
 Your First 90 Days 
 Days 1–30: Learn the client journey, tools, account history, and existing team workflows.
 Days 31–60: Begin managing about 10–20 accounts on your own, set up regular check-ins, and track account health.
 Days 61–90: Work toward full portfolio ownership, report on retention health, and recommend process improvements.
 Earning Potential 
 Base: USD $60,000–$70,000 per year.
 Variable: Performance incentives are mainly tied to quarterly client retention, with additional bonuses for client testimonials. Detailed retention bonus tiers will be shared before the offer stage.
 Target OTE: The total target earning opportunity is approximately USD $80,000–$90,000 per year, negotiable based on experience. Earnings above base depend on performance and are not guaranteed.

 Excellent spoken and written English, with confident client communication.
 Empathy, sound judgment, and a strong sense of ownership.
 Strong organization and follow-through while managing multiple accounts and competing priorities.
 Proactive problem-solving and comfort working with distributed teams in a fast-moving environment.
 Ability to understand basic marketing performance reports and explain practical next steps to clients.

This position designs, builds, and maintains Power BI reports and data models, writes and tunes the SQL beneath them, and maintains the Crystal Reports used for operational and printed reporting. Working alongside two full stack developers - one on the front end used by the shop floor, one on the back end and administrative side - and a project coordinator, this position complements in-house web and software development with the business intelligence layer that sits above it, and provides reporting, communication, and design support to the project as a whole.  Design, build, and maintain Power BI reports, dashboards, datasets, and data
 models for management and senior management, including scheduled refreshes,
 gateway configuration, and workspace access.
 Write, review, and tune the SQL beneath all reporting, including queries, views, and
 stored procedures against the ERP and in-house application databases.
 Develop and maintain Crystal Reports for operational and printed reporting and support the users who depend on them.

À propos du poste

HTS Assist est l'assistant d'intelligence artificielle agentique de Hopper pour le voyage, qui résout de vrais enjeux clients comme les changements de vol, les annulations, les remboursements et les réservations, par clavardage et par la voix, pour certaines des plus grandes marques et entreprises de voyage au monde. La voix pose ses propres défis produit, de la latence et de l'alternance de la parole jusqu'au moment de l'escalade vers un humain, et ce poste couvre les deux volets avec la même rigueur. 

À titre de directeur ou directrice principal(e) de produit, vous serez responsable de l'agent orienté client de bout en bout : les conversations, l'interface et l'expérience que nos partenaires offrent à des millions de voyageurs. Il s'agit d'un poste délibérément axé sur le design, où vous serez la personne qui tranche les décisions de design au quotidien, en façonnant directement les parcours et les interfaces en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de design de nos partenaires et notre designer interne.


À quoi ressemblerait votre quotidien

 - Être responsable de la feuille de route de l'agent conversationnel orienté client, tant par clavardage que par la voix, de la couverture des intentions et de la conception des conversations jusqu'aux interfaces que nos partenaires intègrent dans leurs applications et leurs sites web

 - Établir la norme produit pour la voix en particulier, en couvrant la latence, l'alternance de la parole, la gestion des interruptions, la localisation, la voix en temps réel et la qualité de la reconnaissance et de la synthèse vocale, puisque la tolérance d'une personne au téléphone envers une mauvaise expérience est plus faible que celle d'une personne qui clavarde

 - Mobiliser les partenaires d'entreprise à travers la découverte, la définition des exigences et les décisions de lancement, en traduisant leurs besoins en choix de produit qui permettent à un seul produit de servir plusieurs partenaires

 - Collaborer avec l'équipe Solutions partenaires sur la mise en œuvre et l'intégration

 - Piloter le design au quotidien, en travaillant directement dans Figma pour produire des parcours et des maquettes, et collaborer avec l'équipe de design sur les livrables haute fidélité et de production

 - Construire des prototypes fonctionnels à l'aide d'outils de codage par IA lorsque cela est plus efficace qu'une spécification écrite, afin de tester des parcours de conversation et des concepts d'interface

 - Définir et défendre les seuils de qualité avec l'équipe d'évaluation, en couvrant le taux de résolution, le taux de confinement, la justesse des escalades et la qualité des conversations

 - Spécifier en détail le comportement de l'agent, y compris la résolution, le ton, la politique d'escalade, les garde-fous et les cas limites, et itérer à partir des données de conversations réelles

 - Rester proche des équipes GTM, Solutions partenaires et Succès client, afin de faire remonter les apprentissages du terrain vers la feuille de route

Le ou la candidat(e) idéal(e) possède

 - 8 ans ou plus d'expérience en gestion de produit, incluant une responsabilité de niveau principal ou de direction sur un produit orienté client, avec une expérience directe du lancement de produits conversationnels vocaux tels que les systèmes IVR, les robots vocaux ou l'automatisation vocale de centres de contact

 - Une responsabilité directe d'un produit vocal en production, pas seulement d'un produit conversationnel par clavardage ou par texte, avec une bonne connaissance des compromis liés à la reconnaissance et à la synthèse vocale, des seuils de latence et de la gestion de l'alternance de la parole ou des interruptions. Il s'agit d'une compétence exigée

 - Une aisance en design, à l'aise de manipuler des fichiers de design et de produire seul(e) des parcours et des maquettes de base dans Figma, ayant déjà agi comme responsable de design de facto au sein d'une petite équipe

 - La capacité d'écrire suffisamment de code pour faire fonctionner un prototype sans attendre un ingénieur ou une ingénieure, en intégrant les outils d'IA comme partie normale de sa façon de construire

 - Une expérience concrète en développement front-end, ayant déjà bâti ou lancé des interfaces web et étant capable d'échanger de façon crédible avec des ingénieurs

 - Une solide expérience auprès de clients d'entreprise, idéalement dans des industries réglementées, à façonner les exigences et les décisions de lancement au niveau du produit

 - Une approche axée sur les données, ancrée dans les mesures de service à la clientèle et d'automatisation, incluant la résolution, le confinement, la satisfaction client et la qualité des escalades

 - Une bonne connaissance pratique des produits basés sur les grands modèles de langage, incluant la conception des invites et des comportements, les pratiques de qualité en IA et leurs modes d'échec

Avantages sociaux

 - Une entreprise en démarrage bien financée et éprouvée, avec de grandes ambitions, un salaire compétitif et les avantages d'un régime d'options avant l'entrée en bourse

 - Hopper couvre 100 % des primes du régime d'assurance collective

 - N'hésitez pas à nous poser des questions sur notre congé parental très généreux

À propos de Hopper 
Chez Hopper, notre mission est de devenir la plateforme de voyage de référence à l'échelle mondiale, en propulsant l'application mobile et le site Web de Hopper ainsi que notre division B2B, HTS. Grâce à d'importantes quantités de données et à des algorithmes d'apprentissage automatique avancés, Hopper combine une offre d'agence de voyages de calibre mondial avec des produits fintech propriétaires pour offrir transparence, flexibilité et économies aux voyageurs du monde entier.

La plateforme Hopper dessert des centaines de millions de voyageurs et continue de gagner des parts de marché partout dans le monde, avec plus de 120 millions de téléchargements. Par l'entremise de HTS, notre division B2B qui représente plus de 75 % de l'entreprise, nous propulsons les canaux directs de partenaires comme Capital One, Nubank, Air Canada et bien d'autres.

About the role
HTS Assist is Hopper's agentic AI assistant for travel, resolving real customer issues like flight changes, cancellations, refunds, and bookings over chat and voice for some of the largest travel brands and enterprises in the world. Voice carries its own product problems, from latency and turn-taking to escalation timing when a human is on the line, and this role owns both surfaces with equal depth.      

As Principal Product Manager, you will own the customer-facing agent end to end: the conversations, the interface, and the experience our partners put in front of millions of travelers. This is a deliberately design-leaning role, and you will be the day-to-day design decision-maker, shaping flows and interfaces directly in close partnership with partner design teams and our in-house designer. 


What would your day-to-day look like

 - Own the roadmap for the customer-facing conversational agent across chat and voice, from intent coverage and conversation design to the interfaces partners embed in their apps and websites

 - Set the product bar for voice specifically, covering latency, turn-taking, barge-in handling, localization, realtime voice and ASR/TTS quality, since a caller's tolerance for a bad interaction is lower than a chat user's

 - Engage enterprise partners through discovery, requirement shaping, and launch decisions, translating partner asks into product choices that keep one product serving many partners

 - Partner with Partner Solutions on implementation and onboarding

 - Drive design daily, working hands-on in Figma to produce flows and wireframes, and partner with design on high-fidelity and production assets

 - Build working prototypes using AI coding tools where they beat a written spec, to test conversation flows and interface ideas

 - Define and defend quality bars with the evaluation team, covering resolution rate, containment, escalation correctness, and conversation quality across both chat and voice

 - Specify agent behavior in detail, including resolution, tone, escalation policy, guardrails, and edge cases, and iterate from production conversation data

 - Stay close to GTM, Partner Solutions, and Success teams, feeding what the field learns back into the roadmap

An ideal candidate has

 - 8+ years of product management experience, including principal or lead-level ownership of a customer-facing product, with direct experience shipping voice-based conversational products such as IVR, voice bots, or contact center voice automation

 - Hands-on ownership of a production voice product, not only chat or text-based conversational AI, with working knowledge of ASR/TTS tradeoffs, latency budgets, and turn-taking or barge-in design. This is a required skillset

 - Design fluency, comfortable manipulating design files and producing flows and basic mocks solo in Figma, having operated as a de facto design lead on a lean team

 - The ability to write enough code to get a prototype working without waiting on an engineer, treating AI tools as a normal part of how they build

 - Hands-on front-end experience, having built or shipped web front ends and able to engage engineers credibly

 - Deep partner-facing experience with enterprise clients, ideally in regulated industries, shaping requirements and launch decisions at the product level

 - A data-driven approach grounded in customer service and automation metrics, including resolution, containment, CSAT, and escalation quality

 - Working familiarity with LLM-based products, including prompt and behavior design, AI quality practices, and their failure modes


Perks and benefits of working with us

 - Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and upsides of pre-IPO equity packages

 - Hopper covers 100% of the premiums for the group insurance plan

 - Hopper offers life, short term and long term disability coverage

 - HSA that covers eligible medical and dental expenses

 - All employees and dependents have access to Dialogue's telemedicine services, anytime, anywhere

 - All employees have access to an RRSP plan with automatic pre-tax withdrawals per pay

 - Please ask us about our very generous parental leave, much above industry standards

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Carrot Cash travel stipend

 - Access to co-working space on demand through FlexDesk and a work-from-home stipend

 - Entrepreneurial culture where pushing limits and taking risks is everyday business

 - Open communication with management and company leadership

 - Small, dynamic teams with massive impact
   

About Hopper
At Hopper, we are on a mission to become the leading travel platform globally, powering Hopper's mobile app, website and our B2B business, HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions). By leveraging massive amounts of data and advanced machine learning algorithms, Hopper combines its world-class travel agency offering with proprietary fintech products to bring transparency, flexibility and savings to travelers globally. We have developed several unique fintech solutions that address everything from pricing volatility to trip disruptions, helping people travel better and save more on their trips.

The Hopper platform serves hundreds of millions of travelers globally and continues to capture market share around the world. The Hopper app has been downloaded over 120 million times and has become largely popular among younger travelers, with 70% of its users being Gen Z and millennials.

While many know us as the Gen Z and Millennial travel app, Hopper has evolved to become much more than that. In recent years, we've grown into a travel fintech provider, commerce platform, and global travel agency that powers some of the world's largest brands.

Through HTS, our B2B division, the company supercharges its partners' direct channels by integrating our fintech products on their sites or powering end-to-end travel portals. Today, our partners include leading travel brands like Capital One, Nubank, Air Canada, and many more.

Here are just a few stats that demonstrate the company's recent growth: billions of dollars worth of travel and travel fintech are sold through Hopper and HTS's channels every year. Our fintech products, including Cancel for Any Reason and Flight Disruption Assistance, have exceptionally strong CSAT because the terms are always clear and customers receive instant, no-questions-asked resolutions. Almost 30% of our app customers purchase at least one fintech product when making a booking, and consumers are 1.6x more likely to repurchase if they add fintech to their booking versus booking travel alone.

Given the success of its fintech products, Hopper launched a B2B initiative, HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), which represents more than 75% of the business. Through HTS, any travel provider, including airlines, hotels, banks, and travel agencies, can integrate and seamlessly distribute Hopper's fintech or travel inventory on their direct channels. As its first HTS partnership, the company partnered with Capital One to co-develop Capital One Travel, a travel portal designed specifically for cardholders. Other HTS partners include Air Canada, Uber, CommBank, Nubank, Flair Airlines and many more.

Hopper has been named the #1 most innovative company in travel by Fast Company. Hopper has been downloaded over 120 million times and continues to see millions of new installs each month. Hopper is now the #3 largest online travel agency in North America, and 70% of our app customers are Gen Z and millennial travelers.

Hopper has raised over $750 million USD of private capital and is backed by some of the largest institutional investors and banks in the world. HTS is primed to continue its growth as the leading travel ecommerce provider in a $1 trillion online shopping category. The Hopper app and website will also continue to be the preferred travel provider for Gen Z and Millennials.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Procurify is the agentic procurement platform that helps mid-market organizations get complete control over their spend. We're trusted by hundreds of companies around the world, across industries like biotechnology, education, health care, manufacturing, and software, to manage over $100B in spend. We're looking for a driven, systems-minded, and execution-focused GTM Campaign Manager to join us on our journey.




ABOUT THE ROLE



As a GTM Campaign Manager, you will architect and operate the campaign systems that convert pipeline strategy into pipeline reality. Working directly under GTM Engineering, you'll build, launch, and continuously optimize the campaigns and targeted lists that feed our go-to-market teams — across every source of pipeline: inbound, outbound, tier/segment, and expansion (cross-sell/upsell).



Think of this role as a regulator's right hand. Procurify's pipeline comes from multiple, interdependent sources, and the business's #1 constraint is total pipeline coverage against our revenue targets. Rather than owning any single channel in isolation, you'll help balance effort dynamically across all of them — surging outbound when inbound softens, activating expansion campaigns against the install base, and calibrating targeting by segment so we maximize total pipeline, not just one number.



We're looking for someone who thinks from first principles — questioning why a campaign, list, or process exists, breaking it down to its fundamentals, and rebuilding it in ways that are simpler, faster, and more scalable. This is not a role for someone who runs one-off campaigns and moves on. We want a systems thinker who sees how targeting, data, messaging, and channels connect — and who designs campaign engines that compound in value over time rather than resetting from zero every quarter. The best campaign is often the one you can systematize and automate away.



This role also sits at the intersection of campaign execution and our evolution as an AI-enhanced platform. You'll champion how AI and automation can eliminate manual list-building, generate and personalize outreach at scale, surface which segments and plays are converting, and free human effort for the highest-leverage pipeline. If you see systems where others see silos, and you believe the best process is one you can automate, you'll thrive here.



We're also looking for someone relentless about the "last mile." Strategy without clean execution and closed-loop communication is worthless — the difference between a booked meeting and a lead sitting untouched. You'll own that last mile as a system: build the list, launch the campaign, hand it off cleanly, communicate it clearly, and measure what actually happened — then feed those learnings back into the engine.



This is not a systems-administration role (that's RevOps), a people-management role (that's BDR leadership), or a strategy-and-budget role (that's Demand Gen leadership). This is the connective tissue that all of those functions rely on but none of them owns: turning targeting, positioning, systems, and AI into campaigns that drive real pipeline.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON:




CAMPAIGN SYSTEMS ACROSS ALL PIPELINE SOURCES

 - Design and operate repeatable, scalable campaign systems — not one-offs — that generate pipeline across inbound, outbound, tier/segment, and expansion.

 - Build and deliver targeted, ICP-aligned lead lists to BDRs proactively and on a repeatable cadence — increasingly automated and AI-generated — as the single most reliable driver of booked meetings.

 - Design, launch, and optimize outbound campaigns end-to-end for both new-business and expansion pipeline, using automation and AI to scale personalization and volume without sacrificing quality.

 - Support inbound performance by iterating and building on systems that improve MQL→SQL conversion.

 - Build expansion (cross-sell/upsell) campaign systems against the existing customer base in partnership with Customer Success and Account Management — a large, under-served pipeline source today.

 - Calibrate campaign targeting by tier/segment (SMB vs. mid-market) to protect and maximize total pipeline, not just a single tier.
   
   


PIPELINE COVERAGE & REBALANCING (UNDER GTM LEADERSHIP)

 - Help monitor pipeline coverage across all sources as a connected system, and reallocate campaign effort to the highest-leverage source as conditions shift.

 - Work from the operational math: track conversion rates by source (MQL→SAL→SQL→pipeline $), model where the leverage is, and use data and automation to drive proactive intervention through GTM led efforts.

 - Flag pipeline softness early, so the business can compensate proactively rather than discovering gaps a quarter too late.
   
   


AI, AUTOMATION & FIRST-PRINCIPLES OPTIMIZATION

 - Apply first-principles thinking to identify and remove friction in how campaigns are built, launched, and handed off — automating the repeatable and reserving human effort for high-value plays.

 - Champion AI and automation across the campaign lifecycle: list generation, enrichment, segmentation, message personalization, sequence optimization, and performance analysis.

 - Continuously deconstruct and rebuild campaign processes to be faster, simpler, and more scalable as we grow.
   
   


LAST-MILE OWNERSHIP & CLOSED-LOOP EXECUTION

 - Ensure clean, automated hand-offs to BDRs and AEs — leads loaded, listed, assigned, and communicated so nothing sits un-worked.

 - Support data fidelity across platforms (Salesforce, Marketo, sequencing, enrichment tools) as a power user of the systems RevOps builds.

 - Define and track measurable outcomes per campaign and per source (SAL, SQL, pipeline $) so "what good looks like" is always explicit — and feed learnings back into the system.
   
   


COLLABORATION & CROSS-SYSTEM ALIGNMENT

 - Partner with Marketing, RevOps, Product Marketing, Sales, BDR leadership, and Customer Success to align targeting, messaging, and campaign execution across the funnel.

 - Apply existing positioning and personas to concrete targeting — and flag when segment/positioning shifts appear to be suppressing high-converting traffic.

 - Work cleanly across teams without owning any of their core mandates — you are the systems builder and connector, not the administrator or the people manager.
   
   


KPIS FOR SUCCESS

 - Increased qualified pipeline creation across all sources (inbound, outbound, tier, expansion), measured in SQLs and pipeline $ — accelerated by AI and automation.

 - Consistent, proactive delivery of high-quality targeted lists to BDRs and AE’s — with measurable lift in meeting production.

 - Improved conversion efficiency across the funnel (session→MQL, MQL→SQL, SAL→SQL).

 - Growth in expansion/upsell pipeline generated through structured, repeatable campaign systems.

 - Reduced manual effort per campaign through automation and systematization.

 - Zero leads lost to poor hand-off — clean, closed-loop execution with no items sitting un-worked.

 - Early, accurate surfacing of pipeline-coverage risk against targets.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 1–3 years in a campaign management, demand generation, sales development, or GTM operations role (or a sharp, high-potential candidate ready to grow into it under mentorship).

 - A systems thinker who sees how people, processes, tools, and data connect — and who designs for scale rather than one-off fixes.

 - A first-principles problem solver who questions assumptions, deconstructs complex processes, and rebuilds them more efficiently.

 - Genuine enthusiasm for AI and automation — with a track record (or strong interest) in using them to eliminate manual work and amplify pipeline output.

 - ICP, persona, and tier fluency — able to independently determine who to target and why, and translate positioning into executable campaign systems.

 - Quantitatively strong — can track conversion rates and pipeline coverage across sources and understand where the leverage is (this is a math + systems + execution role, not execution alone).

 - Proactive, closed-loop communicator — flags blockers early and asks for help rather than silently stalling.

 - Comfortable rebalancing priorities as conditions change; thrives in ambiguity with strong organization.

 - Working knowledge of CRM (Salesforce) and sales/marketing automation (Marketo, Outreach/sequencing, enrichment tools like ZoomInfo/Clay).

 - Strong project management, organization, and communication skills, with an impeccable eye for detail.

 - Bonus: Experience in high-growth SaaS; familiarity with Gong, Clay, ZoomInfo, AI/automation tooling, or enablement platforms.
   
   

For customer-facing or GTM roles, maintains an up-to-date LinkedIn profile and ensures it is refreshed upon joining, to reflect their role at Procurify and help maintain a consistent, professional presence across our GTM team.




WHY PROCURIFY?




HELP US MODERNIZE SPEND MANAGEMENT

 

Procurify is redefining how organizations manage spend - transforming a historically manual, reactive process into a strategic advantage. Today, hundreds of companies trust us to manage billions in spend, and we’re just getting started.

 

Powered by our $50M Series C funding, we are actively expanding our core offering, launching new payment capabilities, and building an AI-enhanced procure-to-pay experience for our customers. Read the press release here https://www.procurify.com/press_release/procurify-raises-50m-series-c/. With fresh investment, a strong product foundation, and big ambitions in AI and payments, we’re entering our next phase of growth. That means a real opportunity to shape what we build, how we scale, and the impact we have on our customers.

 

The best part? The team. We’re a group of builders who move fast, think big, and show up for each other. No egos, no passengers, just people who want to do great work and win together.

 

If you’re looking for a place where you can make a real impact alongside a team that raises the bar, you’ll fit right in.

 


BE EMPOWERED TO DO YOUR BEST WORK

We’ve created an environment where personal and professional growth is a real priority. Some of the great perks we offer include:

 

 - Flexible working: We’re a remote-first organization with flexible working hours. Work anywhere from within Canada! And US if applicable.

 - Responsible time off: We offer a flexible approach to time off; we trust our team to take the time they need to rest and recharge while staying accountable to their commitments.

 - Extended health benefits: We prioritize our team’s health and well-being. We offer a competitive health, vision, and dental package along with an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and a health and wellness spending account.

 - Continuous Learning: We host regular educational lunch and learns to help our team grow, share knowledge, and stay curious.

 - Stock options: Everyone has a chance to own a part of Procurify with our competitive stock program.

   This range is dependent on experience, with a component of these earnings made up of a Company Incentive Plan (CIP) target of 5% of base salary, and not inclusive of any benefits or equity that might exist in your total compensation package.



 


LEARN MORE

Procurify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate against any team members or applicants for employment because of race, color, disability, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, or gender identity and/or expression.

 Preferred Experience

 Home improvement
 Building products

 Contractors and installers
 Consumer electronics
 Hospitality and hotels

 Dealer or distributor networks

 Experience selling

 MOTORYSE demo kit and product samples
 Dealer portal access
 Co-branded marketing materials
 Product training videos
 Proposal templates
 Referral tracking for every dealer you sign
 One-week onboarding program covering product knowledge, CRM setup, sales process, and live demo training
 Direct access to company leadership
 A ground-floor opportunity to help build a national dealer channel
 Unlimited earnings potential 
 Why Join MOTORYSE

 Hospitable.com is a remote-only and fully distributed company. We hire based on timezones.
 What you will be working on
 Your mission is to help our customers build more successful short-term rental businesses while driving revenue growth for Hospitable.
 This isn't a traditional Customer Success role focused primarily on answering questions, managing relationships, or preventing churn. We're building a proactive, commercially driven Success team that helps customers discover opportunities, get more value from our platform, and grow their businesses.
 You'll own a revenue quota, and your ability to consistently meet or exceed that quota will be the primary measure of your success. 
 You'll do this through the following:
 Revenue Growth & Expansion: Own and achieve quarterly revenue targets through subscription upgrades, annual conversions, feature adoption, and additional products and services. You'll proactively identify opportunities within our existing customer base and turn those conversations into measurable revenue.
 Consultative Selling: Get to know our customers, their businesses, and what they're trying to accomplish. Whether they're managing one property or hundreds, you'll identify opportunities to help them save time, increase revenue, and operate more efficiently using Hospitable.
 Proactive Customer Engagement: Don't wait for customers to reach out. You'll actively engage customers through scheduled meetings, personalized outreach, and targeted campaigns to uncover opportunities, demonstrate value, and drive action.
 Product Adoption & Monetization: Help customers discover and adopt features that can make a meaningful difference in their businesses, including Direct Booking, Dynamic Pricing, Upsells, and other revenue-generating tools. You'll connect product capabilities to real business outcomes and identify opportunities to expand their investment in Hospitable.
 Customer Education & Workshops: Lead engaging 1:1 consultations, group workshops, and product demonstrations that help customers get more from Hospitable. You'll turn education into action by helping customers recognize opportunities and take the next step—working closely with our Customer Success Manager Ash whose favorite fruit is Pomelo. 
 Strategic Account Management: Work with high-value customers through Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and ongoing conversations to understand their goals, identify gaps in their current setup, and develop recommendations that support their growth and expand their use of Hospitable.
 Pipeline & Performance Ownership: Build and manage your own pipeline of opportunities, maintain accurate CRM records, and consistently follow through on customer conversations. You'll be responsible for your activity, pipeline health, forecasting, and ultimately your results.
 Customer Advocacy & Collaboration: Bring customer feedback, challenges, and ideas back to our product and support teams. You'll work closely with teammates to help customers succeed while identifying new opportunities for Hospitable to deliver value.
 What success looks like 
 We believe great Customer Success Managers create value for customers and measurable growth for the company.
 You'll be successful in this role when you're consistently achieving your revenue quota, building a healthy pipeline of opportunities, helping customers adopt valuable features, and turning customer conversations into meaningful business outcomes.
 We give our team the autonomy to own their results. You'll have support, tools, and coaching along the way, but we expect you to take initiative, find opportunities, and be accountable for your performance.
 If you love helping people, enjoy the challenge of selling, and get excited about being rewarded for the results you deliver, you'll feel right at home here.
 For this position, your location is not a requirement. The ideal fit would work under North American timezones.

 Problem-Solving & Adaptability: You're resourceful, comfortable working independently, and willing to try new approaches when something isn't working. You see challenges as opportunities to learn and improve.
 Team Collaboration: You enjoy sharing ideas, learning from others, and working with cross-functional teams. You're competitive with your own goals while being genuinely invested in the success of the team.
 Experience in short-term rentals, hospitality technology, property management, or revenue management is a plus, but not required.
 The company itself is also a product, one that we iterate on. We're always improving and creating an environment where we all love to work.
 A supportive, radically transparent, and caring team environment, where you are trusted, not managed—and a culture that is focused on results and output.

Media buying is now the easy part. 
 In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right.
 So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.
 Here's what "end to end" actually means here.
 You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.
 You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.
 You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like
 Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.
 Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.
 Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.
 Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.
 Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.
 Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
 You're a fit if
 You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.
 You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.
 You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.
 You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.
 You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.
 You're not a fit if
 "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 Why This Role Is Exciting
 This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets.  We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You will grow into senior strategy.  We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Full Stack Engineer (.NET + Front-End) — NetSpeek 
 NetSpeek is the agentic control plane for enterprise physical infrastructure . We govern how AI agents reason about, decide on, and execute actions across enterprise endpoints. Our reasoning and execution layer — Lena — sits in customer production environments, where reliability, observability, and auditability are non-negotiable.
 TThe Full Stack Engineer ships features end-to-end across the .NET backbone, the React surfaces, and the operator workflows on top of Lena. You'll move across the stack daily.
 What you'll work on
 Designing and shipping .NET 6+ backend services that mediate between AI reasoning, device adapters, and operator surfaces.
 Building React surfaces that present Lena's signal — including uncertainty shape, not just confidence numbers.
 Owning the REST API design between backend and frontend (and Lena's Python services).
 Driving operator UX decisions in partnership with product, with attention to the workflows operators run dozens of times a day.
 You're a fit if 
 You have 5+ years of .NET / C# backend experience, with hands-on production work in .NET 6 or newer.
 You have 3+ years of React (or comparable modern framework) experience.
 You've shipped end-to-end features that touched both backend and frontend in the same project.
 You've designed and shipped production REST APIs in a distributed SaaS environment.
 You have hands-on production experience with AWS (preferred), Azure, or GCP.
 You probably aren't a fit if 
 You're a backend-only engineer who treats the UI as someone else's problem.
 You're a frontend-only engineer who treats the API as a given.
 You haven't worked in environments where AI changes the contract between layers..
 How to apply
 We prefer applications through our hiring site: https://build.netspeek.ai/roles/full-stack-engineer 
There are three paths there, and we prioritize them in this order: 
1. Incident Lab / Case Study —work through a real scenario for this role and send your reasoning with the application. Read first. The scenario gives us the most signal on how you actually think. 
2. Field Note —a single written take instead of the scenario. Read second. Faster than the lab, still a strong signal. 
3. Standard application —resume and the basics through the site's apply form. Read third. Applying directly through Workable below also works, and we'll still read it. The site's three paths exist because they give us better context for the read.
 Either path is read by a human on our hiring team. No AI scoring, no auto-rejection.
 Read the Engineering Handbook and How We Evaluate before applying.
After an offer
 We run standard pre-employment checks before your start date: identity verification, right-to-work confirmation, employment verification, and (where lawful and role-relevant) a criminal record check. We don't run credit checks or online reputation scoring. 
 Must-have
 Strong backend engineering experience in .NET / C#, with hands-on production work in modern .NET (6+, not legacy Framework only).
 Frontend development experience with modern React (or comparable framework such as Next.js, Vue, or Svelte).
 API design experience for distributed SaaS systems; you have designed and shipped production REST APIs.
 Cloud-native application development with AWS preferred (Azure or GCP also welcome).
 Strong debugging and systems thinking.
 Strong signal
 Real-time systems or orchestration platform experience.
 Enterprise SaaS architecture familiarity.
 Exposure to AI-integrated applications (you do not need to be the AI engineer, but you should be comfortable working alongside one).
 Startup or scale-up environment experience.
 Observability and operational tooling familiarity.
 We are growth-stage and fully remote, not late-stage. We invest in the work, the tools, and the people, not the manifesto.
 What that looks like in practice:
 Flexible / unlimited time off
 Health insurance
 Equity participation, discussed at offer
 Fully remote
 Architectural ownership of work that ships to real enterprise customers
 Direct working relationships with the people setting platform strategy
 A growth-stage platform where the decisions you make in your first year shape the product for years
 AI-assisted tooling licensed by NetSpeek (Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or comparable)

 AI architecture standards as code. Define the enterprise AI reference architecture and approved patterns. Encode them as harness skills, agent constitutions and automated fitness checks, so standards apply at generation time rather than at review.

 Claio is a Montréal-based AI platform built for dental and healthcare practices. More than 400 practices across North America use Claio to answer patient calls, fill their schedules, and cut time spent on clinical notes. Clinicians report saving an average of 8+ hours a week on documentation.

 AI Front Desk: answers patient calls 24/7, including nights and weekends. It books and reschedules appointments directly in the practice management system and hands calls to staff when needed.

About Portless
 Portless is a dynamic and innovative 3PL provider revolutionizing how businesses manage their Direct Supply Chain. We help merchants deliver a seamless post-purchase experience through fast, reliable fulfillment and logistics—so they can grow with confidence.
 About the Role 
 As a Customer Success Manager, you will own a portfolio of merchants and drive the full customer success flywheel: Adopt → Realize Value → Expand → Renew with Confidence This is not a "ticket routing" role. You are a strategic partner in your merchant's growth. You will be accountable for customer outcomes by proactively driving adoption, identifying paths to improve operational performance, and introducing services that deepen value. You will bridge the gap between merchant goals and operational reality, ensuring our delivery is both successful and scalable.
 What You’ll Own (Responsibilities)
 1. Adoption & Enablement
 Lead Post-Launch Success: Ensure merchants reach operational "go-live" and early stability through rigorous success plans.
 Drive Feature Adoption: Align merchant objectives with Portless capabilities to ensure they are utilizing the full potential of our platform.
 2. Value Realization & Outcomes
 KPI Operationalization: Define success for each account (speed, cost, delivery experience) and translate it into measurable performance metrics.
 Proactive Health Monitoring: Use leading indicators like volume trends and exception rates to prevent issues before they impact the merchant.
 Strategic Business Reviews: Lead MBRs/QBRs that prove value and align on priorities for the upcoming quarter.
 3. Expansion via Services & Upsells (Expand)
 Outcome-Driven Solutioning: Identify opportunities to improve merchant growth through value-added services such as order protection and inventory financing.
 Build Business Cases: Conduct discovery and scope solutions that demonstrate clear ROI for the merchant.
 Repeatable Expansion Plays: Contribute to internal playbooks for service-led growth.
 4. Renewal & Risk Leadership
 Forecasting & Mitigation: Identify churn risks early and build internal alignment to deliver risk mitigation plans.
 Escalation Management: Act as the senior point for complex concerns, driving root cause identification and corrective actions.
 5. Cross-Functional Leadership
 Internal Advocacy: Be the "voice of the merchant" while balancing operational constraints; drive accountability across Operations, Product, and Engineering.
 Feedback Loops: Identify recurring friction and provide structured feedback to the Product team to influence the roadmap.
 Success Metrics (What “Good” Looks Like)
 Retention: Gross Retention Rate and Churn Risk Reduction.
 Adoption: Achievement of early-stage adoption milestones.
 Growth: Service attach rate and influenced upsell pipeline.
 Qualifications
 Fluent in English: Exceptional written and spoken communication for an executive audience.
 3+ Years in Customer Success: Proven experience owning renewals and growth outcomes in a relatable AM/CS role.
 Domain Expertise: Strong fulfillment, shipping, or e-commerce operations knowledge (3PL experience strongly preferred).
 Analytical Mindset: Able to interpret operational data, find trends, and turn insights into action plans.1
 Selling Comfort: Experience with services-led discovery and value articulation.
 Values & Ways of Working
 Extreme Ownership: A "Merchant-First" mentality with a kind-and-caring team orientation.
 Judgment & Precision: Knows when to be strategically bold and when to be operationally precise.
 Scalability: Focuses on building repeatable systems rather than one-off heroics.6
 Ideal Candidate Profile 
 You are tired of "surface-level" CS roles and want to own the entire lifecycle of a physical product’s journey. You are a systems-thinker who hates "one-off heroics" and would rather build a playbook that solves a problem for 100 merchants at once. You are strategically bold enough to challenge a merchant's assumptions but operationally precise enough to ensure their packages arrive on time.
